title: pkix-chain Error::ProfileViolation and OcspDelegation use Cow<'static, str>
description:
In pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:173-209, Error::ProfileViolation and Error::OcspDelegation carry a reason: Cow<'static, str> field. The rustdoc says 'Cow<'static, str> rather than &'static str so the serde deserialize path can yield an owned String'. All producers use Cow::Borrowed from &'static str literals, and consumers are told to 'pattern-match on the variant rather than the inner string'.

What goes wrong: The reason field looks like structured data but is actually a fixed set of static strings used as an ad-hoc enum. Callers who want to programmatically distinguish profile violations (e.g., 'EKU not critical' vs. 'EKU not sole') must string-match. Adding a new kind of profile violation requires a new &'static str literal but no type-system help.

Location: pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:173-209

Recommendation: Consider replacing the Cow<'static, str> reason with a dedicated ProfileViolationKind enum whose Display impl produces the current string text. This preserves programmatic matching and serde round-trip while removing the string-matching antipattern.
